entries.what_happened: The same source-export-scanning logic was independently reimplemented in 2 different governance scripts (scripts/build-arch-book.ts's extractExportsFromFile, scripts/sync-registry.ts's extractExports) instead of one shared function. Both then independently had the identical class of bug (glob missing .tsx, `export default function Name` mishandled) discovered and fixed on 3 separate occasions across this session (Phase 2.3B fixed build-arch-book.ts's glob+target-resolution; DNA-000023 discovered sync-registry.ts had the exact same glob bug, never fixed; DNA-000023 then found build-arch-book.ts's SIBLING function extractExportsFromFile had a third, different instance of the same bug family — generic "default" string instead of the real export name).
entries.root_cause: No single shared, tested utility for 'what does this TS/TSX file export' — each governance script grew its own regex-based copy. A fix applied to one copy was never propagated to the other, because nothing links them or flags the duplication.
entries.lesson: When two tools parse the same kind of source construct (imports, exports, layer boundaries) with independently-maintained regex/parsing logic, they will drift out of sync. The fix is either a shared utility module, or — if kept separate for isolation reasons — an explicit cross-reference comment in both files pointing at each other so a fix in one prompts a check of the other.
entries.detection_note: No mechanical check exists for 'two files implement similar parsing logic and have drifted.' This class of bug requires code-review judgment, not a regex gate — documented here honestly rather than claiming a false mechanical guard. scripts/build-arch-book.ts:58 and scripts/sync-registry.ts:44 both now carry a code comment cross-referencing each other and this KM-001 entry, so a future editor of one is prompted to check the other.

entries.root_cause: Nothing checked, at the time either second implementation was created, whether a file with the same or a conceptually-equivalent name/responsibility already existed elsewhere in the repo.
entries.lesson: Before creating a new module whose basename or stated purpose matches something that might already exist, search the repo for that name/responsibility first. This is mechanically checkable — same basename in 2+ different directories is a strong, real signal.
entries.detection_note: DNA-000026: Guard 9 in scripts/pre-commit-check.sh — general basename-collision heuristic across all source files, WARN only (real false-positive rate for generic names, e.g. session.ts/timeline.ts). DNA-000027 (Rule 100 full pipeline propagation) added evidence-CONFIRMED-pair enforcement, read from the single source registry/existence.json known_mistakes.confirmed_duplicate_pairs by 3 separate scripts rather than hardcoded per-script: (1) Module Registration — scripts/sync-registry.ts warns the moment a new file matching either side of a confirmed pair is first registered; (2) Dependency Validation — scripts/check-imports.sh REJECTs (exit 1) if any file imports the deprecated side of a confirmed pair; (3) Architecture Validation — scripts/build-arch-book.ts marks a deprecated:true module BROKEN if it regains a real importer, contradicting its own status. entries.what_happened: While building and verifying SDRN-P3 (running `npm run build` to prove a new client component/API route actually compiled), the real build output listed routes never found by any prior audit this session, including the extensive SDRN-P2 'unified runtime model' discovery pass 2 turns earlier: app/api/self-description/route.ts (real, reads core/runtime/self-awareness.ts — fine) and a public app/api/v1/* surface (capabilities, drivers, modules, query, spec, workflows, constitution) meant for external AI to query DNA OS. Checking each: /api/v1/capabilities, /api/v1/modules, /api/v1/drivers correctly read real registry/*.json files. But /api/v1/workflows imports '@/07-workflow-registry.json' — one of the stale, pre-reorg, zero-real-importer root-level files already flagged as non-authoritative in DNA-000024/025 — meaning a real, public, external-facing API endpoint has been serving stale/wrong workflow data, not the real 19-workflow registry (registry/commands/workflows.json). And /api/v1/constitution hardcodes its own separate copy of the Constitution as a literal object in the route file, using old pre-reorg V1-V6 terminology (explicitly forbidden by CLAUDE.md's own 'เดิมคือ V1-Input/...V6-Executor...ห้ามใช้ชื่อเดิม' rule), instead of reading registry/CONSTITUTION.json — so it is both stale and a second, undeclared duplicate of the Constitution (the exact pattern Rule 101 exists to prevent), not caught by any duplicate-detection built so far because Guard 9/confirmed_duplicate_pairs only compare file basenames, not a hardcoded object against a JSON file's content.
entries.root_cause: Two compounding causes: (1) SDRN-P2's 'System Discovery' pass enumerated known self-description mechanisms by name (existence-intelligence, self-awareness, cockpit, etc.) rather than exhaustively walking app/api/** for every route — a real, undiscovered public API surface was missed because discovery was driven by a checklist, not a full filesystem scan. (2) These 2 specific routes were each built by independently copying/hardcoding data instead of importing the real registry file, so they silently drifted the moment the source of truth changed (the reorg, and Rule 100/101/102's additions to CONSTITUTION.json).
entries.lesson: A 'unified model' discovery pass that works from a list of known subsystem names, however thorough that list feels, is not the same as an exhaustive scan — this session's own SDRN-P2 missed a real, live, public API surface. Future discovery passes should include a literal directory walk (e.g. `find app/api -name route.ts`) as a cross-check against whatever checklist is being used, not rely on the checklist alone. Separately: any API route that duplicates registry content by copying it into the route file instead of importing the real file will eventually drift — this is a specific, checkable instance of Rule 101 that current tooling (Guard 9, confirmed_duplicate_pairs) does not catch, since it compares file names, not content-vs-registry consistency.
entries.detection_note: No mechanical check exists for 'this API route's hardcoded/imported data has drifted from the real registry it should represent.' Found by chance while verifying an unrelated build (SDRN-P3), not by any systematic check.

entries.what_happened: The Validation Result Ledger (registry/VALIDATION_RESULTS.json, DNA-000050) recorded PASS/FAIL correctly, but every single FAIL entry (VR-000002 Pre-commit Guards, VR-000003 knip, VR-000004 jscpd, VR-000007 Dependency Graph — 4/4, 100%) had root_cause, evidence, and suggested_fix all null. Found by analyzing the ledger itself, per owner MISSION: "ใช้ Validation Result Ledger ที่สะสมไว้ วิเคราะห์หา รูปแบบความผิดพลาดที่เกิดซ้ำ".
entries.root_cause: scripts/governance.sh's run_check() ran `eval "$cmd" 2>&1` directly inside the if-condition, streaming the real command output straight to the terminal — nothing was ever captured into a variable, so record-validation.ts was called on every FAIL with no --evidence flag at all, and had nothing real to report.
entries.lesson: A capability that records WHETHER something failed is not the same as one that records WHY — without capturing real output at the point of failure, a Validation Result Ledger degrades into a pass/fail counter with the diagnostic fields permanently empty. Any future recorder-style capability must capture and pass real evidence at the source, not leave it to be filled in later (it never was).
entries.detection: scripts/record-validation.ts now WARNs on every FAIL recorded without --evidence (mechanical, not manual) — see governance.sh's run_check(), fixed at the source in the same pass (DNA-000051) to capture real command output and pass it as --evidence automatically.

entries.title: Audit Self Feedback Loop
entries.what_happened: registry/VALIDATION_RESULTS.json (an append-only Runtime Validation ledger) was scanned by the same audit tools it was meant to record the results of — Guard 1's grep (Supabase-URL scan) and jscpd (Duplicate Detector) — causing its own past --evidence text to be re-matched and fed back in as new evidence every governance.sh run, growing unboundedly (44 entries/54KB) and inflating the reported clone count 274 -> 300 across two runs in the same audit.
symptom: Clone Count increases every run (274 -> 300 observed)
Validation ledger (registry/VALIDATION_RESULTS.json) grows continuously (54KB and climbing)
governance.sh's own pipeline crashes with 'tr: Illegal byte sequence' once evidence text got long enough
root_causes: Guard 1's grep scanned *.json broadly with no exclusion for the ledger file it was itself writing to
jscpd's CLI invocation in governance.sh/dashboard.sh passed explicit directory args that silently overrode .jscpd.json's own format/ignore config, scanning the ledger's JSON content anyway
(related, separately discovered) tail -c 1800 cut at a raw byte offset, sometimes slicing a multi-byte Thai character in half, which tr then rejected under the default locale
entries.root_cause: Evidence (a runtime-generated ledger) was treated as Source (scannable audit input) by two different tools, with no isolation boundary between the two — a structural gap, not a one-off typo.
prevention: Exclude the ledger from Guard 1's scan (basename-only exclude pattern — grep's --exclude matches basename, not full relative path)
Explicitly pass -f/-i flags to jscpd's CLI invocation so it cannot silently diverge from .jscpd.json
Separate Source Zone and Evidence Zone as a named Constitution concept (Rule 107), not just an ad hoc fix
Use LC_ALL=C when truncating real command output at a byte offset before piping into tr
verification: Clone count stable and correct across repeated real runs (97, not 274/300)

Ledger growth normal after the fix — 11 clean entries -> 22 after one real governance.sh run, all evidence lengths bounded and matching the first clean run exactly (564/1800/1086/492 chars, no recursion)
governance.sh completes end to end with zero 'Illegal byte sequence' occurrences
Evidence Isolation Guard (scripts/check-evidence-isolation.sh) deliberately regressed and confirmed it catches the exact failure mode, then restored
entries.lesson: A validation/audit system that records its own results must have an explicit, enforced boundary between the files it WRITES (evidence) and the files it READS as input (source) — without that boundary, any tool with a broad enough scan pattern will eventually treat its own output as new input, and the corruption compounds silently until something else (a crash, a suspicious statistic) surfaces it.
entries.detection: partial mechanical — scripts/check-evidence-isolation.sh (Guard 12) checks the 2 known real violators (Guard 1, jscpd) stay excluded; scripts/verify-environment.sh (Rule 109) checks tool identity before trusting audit results
entries.detection_note: Guard 12 is pattern-based and bounded to the known Evidence Zone files and known scan commands — it would not automatically catch a brand-new audit tool added later that also fails to exclude the Evidence Zone; that still relies on Rule 107 being applied by whoever adds it, same honesty pattern as KM-001/102/103.

entries.architectural_knowledge: A Deno Edge Function helper module (9 exports: ConversationState, getOrInitState, updateConversationState, extractEntities, saveEntitiesToRegistry, executeBusinessValidation, checkBusinessQualification, extractStructuredEntitiesWithGemini, resolveAddressToCoordinates) implementing a full stateful conversation-flow architecture: a conversation_states table row per LINE user, regex-based Thai NLU for intent/entity detection (material, quantity, vehicle type, concrete grade, tax ID, destination, contact info), a 2-level business validation gate (field-completeness, then business qualification), and a Gemini API fallback for structured extraction and geocoding.
entries.business_knowledge: Built to let a customer request a concrete/aggregate quote entirely through LINE chat, tracking a multi-turn conversation until enough fields were captured to price and qualify the order — matches this project's real business domain (ready-mix concrete / aggregate logistics dispatch via LINE, confirmed via the Thai regex vocabulary: ดินถม/ทรายหยาบ/หินคลุก/เหล็กข้ออ้อย, vehicle types 6-wheeler/10-wheeler/trailer, ksc concrete grades).
entries.dependency_relationships: Imports @/../_shared/haversine.ts (distance calc) and reads/writes real Supabase tables: conversation_states, entity_registry, material_types, pit_materials, pit_profiles, app_configs. Zero real importers anywhere in the codebase — confirmed via grep including within its own directory (supabase/functions/line-webhook-v2/index.ts and every handlers/*.ts file), not just a repo-wide check.
entries.runtime_behavior: Was designed to run inside the line-webhook-v2 Edge Function on every inbound LINE text/location message, mutating conversation_states and returning a Thai-language prompt for whatever field was still missing, escalating to a live price estimate once material+location+quantity were known.
entries.replacement_successor: supabase/functions/line-webhook-v2/handlers/text.ts (the real, live text-message handler) uses a completely different architecture instead: ResponseGateway (engines/response.ts) + tryRouteToTool (engines/tool-router.ts) + tryCompleteAwaitingEvent (engines/event-followup.ts) + tryAutoBuildEvent (engines/auto-build-event.ts) + tryFollowUpDebtAck (engines/debt-followup.ts) — none of which reference conversation_states, ConversationState, or extractEntities. This is a real, confirmed architectural replacement, not a guess.
entries.failure_reason: Not a bug or a mistake — a superseded design. The regex-based intent/entity/state-machine approach was replaced by a tool-routing + event-building architecture at some point before this session; the old file was simply never deleted after the new handlers/text.ts wiring landed.
entries.lessons_learned: A full, working, non-trivial feature (multi-turn conversational quoting) can go completely dark with zero errors or warnings when its caller is quietly rewired to a different architecture — nothing in this codebase's tooling would have caught this without the file-by-file reading done for this Rule 104 pass. Reinforces Rule 104's own premise: orphaned code needs active knowledge extraction, not just a status flag.
